notes: DRAFT for scholarly review; nothing here is reviewed or published. English only: Arabic and Urdu texts are left null for translators. Written from the Quran text in content/quran (Tanzil Uthmani) in the drafter's own words; no published translation is quoted. Quran only: no hadith, no tafsir, no later tradition in the story texts. The occasions of revelation (who the persons were, what happened) are not in the verses; they appear only under unknowns and uncertainties, as later tradition, with the hadith to add later. Pronouns the Arabic leaves open are left open. Chapters are a reading order, not a chronology. Honorifics are added when the page is rendered.

claims.statement_en: The likeness of Isa with God is like the likeness of Adam: God created him from dust, then said to him "Be", and he was.
The truth is from the Lord of the one addressed, so he is not to be among the doubters.

The one addressed is told that if anyone argues with him about him after the knowledge that has come to him, he is to say: come, let us call our sons and your sons, our women and your women, ourselves and yourselves.
Then let them earnestly supplicate, and put the curse of God upon the liars.

chapters.summary_md: The verses say that the likeness of Isa with God is like the likeness of Adam [c1], and that the truth is from the Lord of the one addressed [c2]. They tell him what to say to anyone who argues with him: let each side call their sons, their women and themselves, and earnestly supplicate, and put the curse of God upon the liars [c3][c4].
chapters.body_md:
The likeness of Isa with God is like the likeness of Adam: God created him from dust, then said to him "Be", and he was [c1]. The truth is from the Lord of the one addressed, so he is not to be among the doubters [c2].

The one addressed is told that if anyone argues with him about him after the knowledge that has come to him, he is to say: come, let us call our sons and your sons, our women and your women, ourselves and yourselves [c3]. Then let them earnestly supplicate, and put the curse of God upon the liars [c4].
chapters.deep_md: The passage begins with a likeness and ends with an invitation [c1][c3]. The pronoun in 'about him' is not resolved in the verse; it can be read as Isa or as the truth stated before it [c3]. The invitation names groups to be called, sons, women and ourselves, and leaves the persons unnamed [c3]. What follows the supplication is a curse upon the liars, and the verse says no more [c4].
chapters.kids_md: The verses say that God made Isa like He made Adam: from dust, then He said "Be", and he was [c1]. They say that the truth is from the Lord [c2]. They tell what to say to those who argue: come, let us call our sons and your sons, our women and your women [c3].
chapters.lessons_md: Educational interpretation (not scripture): One reading is that the passage meets an argument with an invitation to turn together to God [c3][c4]. Another is that it begins from a likeness, Isa and Adam, before it turns to the invitation [c1][c3].
chapters.unknowns_md:
- Not established: who argued, where, or when. The verse says 'anyone who argues with you about him'.
- Not established: whether the invitation was carried out, who came, or how it ended; the verses do not say.
- Not established: who 'our sons', 'our women' and 'ourselves' refer to.
- The pronoun in 'about him' (3:61) is read in more than one way; the draft does not decide.
- Named in later tradition, not in the Quranic text: the people who argued, the people called, the place and the occasion. None is used in the story texts.

uncertainties_en: Hadith to add later: authenticated reports on the occasion of the invitation, on those who argued and on those who were called, each with a named grader. None is used in this draft.
The inventory title calls the passage the invitation to mutual invocation; the verses state the invitation and say nothing of its outcome.
The pronoun in 'about him' (3:61) is left open; see the unknowns.
Arabic and Urdu texts are not written; they are left null for translators.
